source.title: Towards Multimodal Interpretability: Learning Sparse Interpretable Features in Vision Transformers

record.tranche_reason: The post qualitatively examines MLP neurons in a modern vision transformer and reports that they appear polysemantic, which challenges the claim that modern architectures yield highly interpretable neurons. It does not test the proposed causes or estimate an interpretable-neuron share.
record.gate_note: The post also reports SAE training losses, sparsity, feature examples and other technical analyses; these do not directly test the claim versions. The neuron-alignment analysis is recorded as a related finding, but cosine alignment does not itself measure whether neurons have one main job.
record.test_reason: In a passing qualitative remark, the post reports that late-layer MLP neurons of a modern vision transformer (CLIP ViT-L, layer 22) all look polysemantic from their top-activating images. This bears weakly on V4's prediction that modern architectures yield mostly interpretable neurons. The study does not vary architecture, regularization or tools, and gives no counts. It is mainly an SAE study.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The author concludes that SAEs find sparse, highly interpretable directions in the CLIP ViT residual stream. A crude analysis finds about half of the features unaligned with neurons and the rest aligned to few neurons (usually under 5). The MLP neurons' top images look polysemantic and much less interpretable than the SAE features.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains an SAE on a CLIP vision transformer and inspects SAE features and their alignment to MLP output vectors; it does not audit neuron poles or test explanations on held-out activations.
record.method_sensitivity: The SAE was trained on ImageNet-1k; the author suspects dataset limitations contribute to issues and proposes training on a much larger dataset. The neuron-alignment analysis is restricted to non-ultra-low-frequency features.

fits_no_version.finding: About half of non-ultra-low-frequency SAE features exceed the random cosine range [0.08, 0.14] to MLP out vectors; the rest do not. No alignment was found with earlier MLP layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In CLIP ViT-L, about half of the residual SAE features align with a few last-layer MLP neurons, and none align with earlier MLP layers.

record.problems: The work studies one model and one residual-stream location, trained on ImageNet-1k; the author calls the neuron-alignment analysis crude. The MLP-neuron interpretability result is qualitative, and no share of interpretable neurons is estimated.

untested.parts: Causes (architecture, regularization, tool quality); any rise in interpretable share with better tools; quantitative shares; the InceptionV1-sized estimates (5% to 99%).
Not tested: language models across scale and MoE.
Not tested: InceptionV1 cat-car neuron and pose explanation.
Not tested: neuron attribution graphs vs replacement models.
Not tested: held-out prediction of explanations from activating examples.

record.verdict_notes: The neuron-polysemanticity remark is a single sentence with no counts, no neuron sample size and no improved tools. The evidence against V4 is therefore weak, and V4 would attribute the result to the weak tool. The SAE was trained on ImageNet-1k only. The relation could arguably be 'discusses'.

versions.untested_parts: The Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit and its stated shares.
Similar shares across language models, dense and mixture-of-experts models, or model sizes up to trillions of parameters.
InceptionV1's cat-and-car neuron, pose, and recursive generalization.

The study tests neuron interpretability qualitatively in one vision model, but does not compare architectures, regularization, or tool quality; estimate a share of interpretable neurons; or test the InceptionV1-sized estimates.
Attribution graphs, behavioural explanations, replacement models, and reconstruction error.
Whether explanations based on activating examples predict firing on held-out activations.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations on new text.

rows.check: 'Reversed' overstates the result. The finding is that interpretable single-job neurons were not seen, which is absence of the predicted effect. The baseline (SAE features more interpretable) compares the study's own method, not a control for V4. The number of neurons inspected is not stated. The tool used is top-activating images, which V4 itself calls weak.

relationships.condition: CLIP ViT-L MLP neurons feeding layer 22 residual stream (class token), judged by top-activating ImageNet images
relationships.reason: Author says the neurons all appear polysemantic, mixing 3-4 unrelated features (r1). A modern architecture alone did not yield clean neurons here, but the weak tool leaves V4's tool explanation open. Qualitative only, with no counts.
relationships.display_finding: The author reports that the neurons all appeared polysemantic, each mixing 3–4 unrelated features, so the modern architecture alone did not give clean neurons. The simple inspection method leaves open the explanation that weak tools are to blame, and the observation is qualitative, with no numbers reported.

tranche.reason: T5 covers results, not only arguments, showing a version needs qualifying. The post's own result (every late-layer MLP neuron in a modern ViT looks polysemantic) qualifies V4's architecture route, which matches the limits_scope verdict. It is weak and qualitative, but it is a result against the version.

statements.correction: Author: the top-activating images of every MLP neuron (layer-22 MLP, CLIP ViT-L) look polysemantic, typically mixing 3 or 4 unrelated features, much less interpretable than the SAE features. Qualitative, no counts, no comparison with other architectures.
statements.problem: The part about this study is right: the top-activating images of every layer-22 MLP neuron look polysemantic, typically 3 or 4 unrelated features. 'Class token' and 'ImageNet images' are implied for the neuron images, not stated. The group's lead sentence ('not more interpretable') is a cross-study reading; this post makes no comparison with older architectures. Other studies' numbers not checked here.
